elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer convenience termination
elements.evidence: No refund language; instead "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed ... unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" — HDI's right operates only to stop renewal at the anniversary, i.e. end of term

elements.element: Customer termination right on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI"

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "provided, that the Termination Payment shall not exceed the payments made to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date"

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination limited to end of a term
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" — HDI can only decline renewal at term end

elements.element: Vendor end-of-term termination on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other"

reasons: All fallback elements are satisfied: an express Customer convenience right at 90 days' notice (within the 60–90 day band), an early-termination fee capped at three months' Section 3.1 payments, and HDI's convenience right confined by the pre-existing renewal mechanic to term end on 90 days' notice.
Preferred is not met: notice is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, only a (now capped) Termination Payment. Consistent with the locked fallback target.

The two edits are narrow — one inserted sentence and one proviso appended to the existing formula; the rest of Section 4.1, including the Net Sales formula and the eight quarterly instalment mechanic, remains effective.

The bracketed gloss "for purposes of this Section 4.1, 'Customer' means the Company" is arguably avoidable (the sentence could have named the Company directly), but it cures an otherwise undefined term and introduces no contradiction, so minimality and intent are preserved.
Margin comment accurately describes the operative changes and cites the playbook cap.
